Resolves #20454

🌿 The window opens with the gesture, so a slow hover can no longer fail the resize.

The resize arm of `HeaderMenuInteractionNL` now opens its 1.8 s `observeMotion` window after `page.mouse.down()`, which leaves the hover and the resize-handle wait outside it. Duration, interval and assertion are unchanged. Both arms attach their motion trace before asserting on it, so a red run keeps its receipt.

Evidence: L3 (local real-Chromium runs through the Bridge fixture: a red-on-base control and a 5× repeat) → L3 required (AC-3, AC-4). No residuals.

Micro-review eligible: test-only — in one spec, the observer's start moves and two attaches move ahead of their assertions; no product source, assertion or threshold changes.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered: the resize arm in `HeaderMenuInteractionNL.spec.mjs` calls `observeMotion` after `page.mouse.down()`, still with `durationMs: 1800, intervalMs: 32` and the same `> box.width + 40` assertion. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: both `testInfo.attach` calls now come before the assertions that read the trace. |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI: with a local-only 1.5 s delay before `page.mouse.down()`, base fails at the samples assertion after every geometry assertion passes, and the fixed spec passes with the same delay (Test Evidence). |
| AC-4 | Outside-CI: the complete spec with `--repeat-each=5 --workers=1`: 25 passed (Test Evidence). |
